The '''1963–64 DDR-Oberliga''' was the 15th season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]].

The league was contested by fourteen teams. [[BSG Chemie Leipzig (1950)|BSG Chemie Leipzig]] won the championship, the club's sole national East German championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 21 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 21 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref> Football in [[Leipzig]] had been reorganised after the 1962–63 season with the two Oberliga clubs from the city, [[FC Sachsen Leipzig|SC Lokomotive Leipzig]] and [[Lokomotive Leipzig|SC Rotation Leipzig]], seeing their playing squads merged and then divided up again. The nominally best players were allocated to the new [[Lokomotive Leipzig|SC Leipzig]] club, later to become 1. FC Lok Leipzig. The nominally weaker players were allocated to [[BSG Chemie Leipzig (1950)|BSG Chemie Leipzig]] which had its Oberliga place returned it had lost to SC Lokomotive in 1954. The fact that the nominally weaker Chemie squad won the league while SC Leipzig only came third is considered to be one of the greatest upsets in the history of East German football.<ref>''fuwo'', page: 24</ref>

Football in [[Chemnitz|Karl-Marx-Stadt]], now Chemnitz, was reorganised, too with the football department of [[FC Erzgebirge Aue|SC Wismut Karl-Marx-Stadt]] returning to [[Aue, Saxony|Aue]] where it had played despite its name and joining BSG Wismut Aue again. SC Wismut Karl-Marx-Stadt then merged with SC Motor Karl-Marz-Stadt to form [[Chemnitzer FC|SC Karl-Marx-Stadt]], now Chemnitzer FC.<ref>''fuwo'', page: 22 & 27</ref>

[[Gerd Backhaus]] of [[1. FC Lok Stendal|BSG Lokomotive Stendal]] was the league's top scorer with 15 goals.<ref name="Goal" >{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 21 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref> For the second time the title [[Footballer of the Year in Germany|East German Footballer of the year]] was awarded, going to [[Klaus Urbanczyk]] of [[Hallescher FC|SC Chemie Halle]].<ref>''fuwo'', page: 92</ref>

On the strength of the 1963–64 title Chemie Leipzig qualified for the [[1964–65 European Cup]] where the club was knocked out by [[Győri ETO FC|Vasas ETO Győr]] in the preliminary round. Eleventh-placed club [[1. FC Magdeburg|SC Aufbau Magdeburg]] qualified for the [[1964–65 European Cup Winners' Cup]] as the seasons [[FDGB-Pokal]] winner and was knocked out by [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray S.K.]] in the first round. Third-placed [[Lokomotive Leipzig|SC Leipzig]] qualified for the [[1964–65 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] where it was knocked out in the first round by [[Wiener Sportclub]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec196465.html |title= European Competitions 1964-65|website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 21 January 2016}}</ref>
